mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is greater than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue growth slows.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not predict negative SPX returns over 60 days (SPX 60-day returns positive in >60% of such periods).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening supply chain capacity and slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not negative during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO declines (returns positive in >50% of such periods).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of retail sales (RSAFS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as stronger consumer spending supports corporate revenue growth and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS is above its 1-year moving average (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE does not predict negative SPX returns over 20 days (SPX 20-day returns positive in >60% of such periods).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rising federal funds rate predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as higher rates compress equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not negative during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS is rising (returns positive in >50% of such periods).
